close_reason: Stability statement added to both the Cargo.toml feature comment and the demo_next_id rustdoc covering: id format is NOT public API; switching feature across minor versions may silently change format; the only guarantees are RFC 8620 §1.2 opacity and within-process collision-freedom; the divergence from canonical mail-server is deliberate (deterministic default makes test debugging easier); do not propagate to siblings.
description:
crate-jmap-calendars-server/Cargo.toml:13-28 declares two cargo features:

- `memory` — documented with explicit stability statement at lib.rs:19-27 and memory.rs:24-27: "API stability is opt-in via this feature and may break across minor versions while the crate is pre-1.0."
- `realistic-demo-ids` — described in the Cargo.toml comment block but with NO equivalent stability statement anywhere in lib.rs or memory.rs.

The `realistic-demo-ids` feature alters runtime behavior of `MemoryBackend::demo_next_id` (memory.rs:387-437): switches from a deterministic per-(type, account) counter to a process-global timestamp-seeded atomic counter. Both modes are "demonstration-quality" per the doc, but a consumer enabling/disabling the feature across minor versions has no documented guarantee about what they can rely on.

Sibling jmap-mail-server has THREE features: `mdn`, `sieve`, `memory`. It has NO `realistic-demo-ids` equivalent. So this is a cookie-cutter divergence: the workspace canonical does not have this feature at all, yet calendars-server adds it without aligning the stability story.

What callers cannot rely on:
- Whether enabling `realistic-demo-ids` across a minor-version bump silently changes the id format (e.g. could a future minor swap "atomic counter base + offset" for "ulid"?).
- Whether the feature is intended to be public (and thus stability-constrained) or internal-test (and thus removable without warning).
- Whether the cookie-cutter divergence is intentional (in which case calendars-server should document why it exists) or accidental (in which case it should be removed and propagated to mail-server first).

Fix options:
1. Add the same stability boilerplate to the realistic-demo-ids feature: at the Cargo.toml comment and inline doc on `demo_next_id`. State explicitly: "Switching this feature on/off between minor versions may change the produced id format silently; downstream consumers MUST NOT depend on a specific id format from MemoryBackend in any case."
2. Or remove the feature, propagate the canonical mail-server pattern (whose `next_id` at email.rs:1748 is the unconditional "realistic" mode).

Option 2 is cleaner. Option 1 leaves the cookie-cutter divergence permanent.
title: realistic-demo-ids feature lacks the stability statement that memory feature has; diverges from mail-server
